meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the RF-CAS-v1 unit
meta.scope: From the gas packs and the ethanol tank to the cold vent and the product tank T-601, including utilities (instrument air, N₂, chilled water, electrical power).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.dev: More feed than the chillers can take
N1.causes:
Cracked-gas section raises the rate
FIC-101 set point raised
FV-101 positioner fails open (FV-101 is fail-closed on air loss only)
N1.cons: Chill temperatures rise, AI-114 rises (ethylene to fuel), compressors run toward maximum power and discharge pressure

N1.causes:
Upstream turndown
FV-101 sticks partly closed
N1.cons: Compressors move toward surge; anti-surge recycle opens and power per tonne rises; chillers over-cool

N1.causes:
XV-100 trips
FV-101 fails closed on air loss
upstream compressor trip
N1.cons: Loss of production; compressors on full recycle; kettles warm slowly — no hazard if both loops keep running

N1.dev: Back-flow from the chilled section to the cracked-gas header
N1.causes: Upstream pressure lost while V-102 is held at 32.5 bar
N1.cons: Cold gas (−35 °C or colder) back into warm carbon-steel piping (brittle fracture), loss of containment

N1.causes: Upstream chiller fouled or cooling water warm
N1.cons: More duty on E-101: propylene level and K-201 power rise; small effect on the off-gas loss

N1.dev: Water or methanol in the feed
N1.cons: Ice and hydrate in E-101 / E-102 tubes and in LV-105 / LV-110: duty falls, valves stick, tube blockage

N1.dev: Feed richer in C2 (more ethylene / ethane)
N1.cons: More liquid in V-101 / V-102; level control must keep up; less load on the ethylene loop (toward surge)
Gas-train pressure rises toward the upstream maximum; E-101 / E-102 tube side, V-101 / V-102 overpressure if their design pressure is below the upstream maximum

sg.text: compressor speed controllers have 12 % reserve above design
UIC-205 / UIC-305 anti-surge recycle (FV-205 / FV-305 fail open)
no check valve credited on the feed line
TIC-102 → LIC-103 cascade raises the level
Dryer outlet moisture analyzer upstream (not on this unit)
no PSHH on the gas train

recs.text: Confirm that the design pressure of the gas train (E-101, E-102, V-101, V-102) covers the maximum upstream pressure; otherwise add PAHH-112 closing XV-100. Consider a check valve on the off-gas line.
Confirm minimum design metal temperatures of all cold equipment and the letdown outlets against the lowest temperature reachable (low suction pressure, cold flash), and alarm accordingly.
Specify the moisture content of refrigerant make-up, dry the loops after maintenance, and add moisture monitoring on the refrigerant charge.
Proof-test the anti-surge valves FV-205 / FV-305 (stroke time) and the surge (vibration) trips; fit discharge check valves.
Agree a communication protocol with the cracked-gas section for rate and composition changes.
Install gas detection and fire protection around the compressors and receivers, with ESD on confirmed gas.
